mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession (UNRATE < 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < previous 12-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when labor market is strong (UNRATE > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% indicates expanding manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO expansion is not followed by positive S&P 500 20-day returns in more than 70% of cases, or the effect disappears during supply-chain disruptions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) drop below 3.5% combined with accelerating wage growth (implied by PAYEMS outpacing population growth) signals a tight labor market, which compresses profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% AND PAYEMS growth > population growth for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% during a recession (UNRATE > 6%) signals an aggressive easing cycle, which supports risk assets and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not statistically different from zero in triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when inflation spikes (CPIAUCSL YoY > 5%).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average by more than 5% suggests households are accumulating cash rather than spending, which reduces near-term consumption and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when consumer confidence is high (not observable, but proxy via HOUST).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in industrial production (INDPRO) and a fall in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% month-over-month signals a shift of capital from construction to manufacturing, which can create sector rotation but overall reduces market breadth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > previous month +2% AND HOUST < previous month -3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong consumer demand (GDPC1 growth > 2% MoM).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage inflation and reduces corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY < 2%).
